# Modelling approach and outcomes

The initial model predictions were:

Previous models used biliary and faecal clearances from and in vivo study, of 0.194 and 0.004 L/d respectively [@fujii2015]. PFOA was modelled to be directly cleared from the liver to gut via the biliary clearance and from the gut to the faeces via faecal clearance. No specific circulation back to the liver was modelled, other than the portal plasma flow.

![](images/clipboard-4158935113.png){width="320"}

![](images/clipboard-1016773992.png){width="320"}

Then I changed the biliary clearance to be only mediated by the BSEP transporter, following michaelis-menten kinetics. As **in vitro** data on the michaelis-menten kinetics of PFOA don't exist, I used data on bile acids, assuming that these reflect the maximum transport capacity of BSEP given that they are the endogenus substrates of the transporter.

This influenced a bit the elimination phase, but not too much.

![](images/clipboard-3143727404.png){width="320"}
